explanation: Computer systems utilize a memory hierarchy to balance speed and cost.  Faster, smaller memories (caches) are placed closer to the processor, while slower, larger memories (main memory) are further away. Effective caching strategies exploit locality of reference (temporal and spatial) to minimize the time spent accessing data.  Understanding and optimizing for the memory hierarchy is crucial for high-performance applications.
syntax: No specific syntax, but cache performance is analyzed through metrics such as miss rate, accesses per iteration, and spatial/temporal locality.
code_example:
; Example illustrating impact of memory access patterns on performance (conceptual)
; Assume a matrix multiplication algorithm is implemented.
; Class AB routines access matrix A column-wise and matrix B row-wise.
; This leads to poor spatial locality (many cache misses).
; Class BC routines access matrices B and C row-wise.
; This leads to better spatial locality (fewer cache misses).
; Performance measurements show significantly faster execution for Class BC routines
; due to reduced cache miss rates for larger array sizes.
example_explanation: The example highlights how different memory access patterns within a matrix multiplication algorithm impact performance.  The Class AB routines exhibit poor spatial locality resulting in numerous cache misses.  The Class BC routines show improved spatial locality, leading to fewer cache misses and consequently faster execution, demonstrating the critical role of caching strategies in performance optimization within the memory hierarchy.
